title: Making and Sharing (implementation choice)
hoursNote: Fourteen forty-minute sessions support the award; they do not supply its whole 35-hour programme. Record actual guided and independent time.
cellsNote: Independent ruled-outcome and week review found no new claim; g29 binds the canonical award plans.

outcomes: Take part in drawing: learn and try controlled line choices. Record what was actually done and an initial learning point. This begins activity one.
lessons.objective: Take part in drawing, try controlled line choices and say what you learnt.

outcomes: Continue the drawing activity with taught tone techniques. Preserve a selected result and the pupil’s account of learning. Identify this as the same activity, not a second one.
lessons.objective: Continue the drawing activity, try ways to make light and dark tones, and explain what you learnt.

outcomes: Take part in a distinct paper-sculpture activity: learn safe folds and ways to make paper stand. Keep a record of participation. This is activity two.
lessons.objective: Take part in paper sculpture, learn safe folds and ways to make paper stand, and record what you learnt.

outcomes: Continue paper sculpture with taught joining/stability techniques. Identify what was learnt in both arts activities, using the pupil’s actual work and words. Do not require numerical improvement for Explore.
lessons.objective: Continue paper sculpture by testing a join, then identify what you learnt in drawing and paper sculpture.

outcomes: Prepare questions and distinguish an artist’s work from an organisation’s role. Read PRACTITIONER_SLOT and ORG_SLOT; keep research/rehearsal labelled preparation. This deck alone does not complete Part B.
lessons.objective: Choose useful questions about an artist and an arts organisation, ready for a live or active experience.

outcomes: Undertake first-hand live/active exploration through the actual route. Record the real artist, activity, what the pupil explored and the evidence location after it happened.
lessons.objective: Take part in a real artist activity and keep a clear record of what you explored.

outcomes: Undertake live/active exploration of the actual organisation and its arts work. Record the organisation’s identity, what the pupil actively explored and its source/experience record. Reading a website alone is preparation.
lessons.objective: Explore an arts organisation through a real activity and show what its work helps people do.

outcomes: Work from actual experience records. Explain or demonstrate what was found about the artist and the organisation and how their roles connect. Check that both are evidenced. Complete a missing live/active element when arranged; do not fill it with an invented account.
lessons.objective: Use real experience records to explain what you found about an artist and an arts organisation, and check both are evidenced.

outcomes: Begin a distinct creation activity. Make the pupil’s own choice of an artwork and accessible tools, informed by previous learning without reusing a finished A/B activity as C. Preserve the starting idea as process evidence.
lessons.objective: Test simple prints and choose a new print-and-collage artwork; preserve the pupil’s starting idea and material trials as process evidence.

outcomes: Teach the needed next technique and begin the chosen artwork. Preserve actual stages through work samples, credited photographs, short notes, or located recordings.
lessons.objective: Begin the pupil’s new print-and-collage artwork using taught overlap and joining steps, and preserve an actual making stage with the pupil’s own choice.

outcomes: Continue making. Teach a useful material/process decision and record what the pupil chose and did. Preserve earlier states before changing them; a ring on overwritten work is not a before-state record.
lessons.objective: Develop the pupil’s new collage through a taught trial of contrast and placement, preserving the earlier state and recording an actual creative choice.

outcomes: Complete the artwork and assemble a trace of its real process. Evidence must contain both process and final work, not only a final image or only a plan.
lessons.objective: Complete the pupil’s new print-and-collage artwork and assemble a trace of its actual making that includes both process evidence and the final work.

outcomes: Look across A–C; pupil chooses personal enjoyment or achievement to communicate, and an accessible format. Prepare/rehearse this distinct sharing activity using the pupil’s own words and choices.
lessons.objective: Look back across Parts A–C, choose your own enjoyment or achievement, and try a clear way to share it with a listener.

outcomes: Actually communicate the chosen enjoyment or achievement. Keep an accurate record of what was communicated and how, with a locator. Check all four part records without presenting a folder audit alone as Part D.
lessons.objective: Share the enjoyment or achievement you chose from looking back at A–C, keep a true record of your message, and check the four part files.
